title: Our Take on a Successful Inbound Recruiting Strategy (September 2026)
summary: Learn how Dover helps early-stage companies build a strong inbound recruiting strategy in September 2026, from job boards to applicant filtering.
body_markdown:
When it comes to[outbound recruiting](https://www.dover.com/) , the difficulty lies in devoting sufficient time and energy into finding, pitching and engaging candidates. Dover cuts down on the time it takes to source, schedule, and craft outreach through automation so that our customers can hire better candidates, faster. We’ve also done the same on inbound. Here’s how.


**TLDR:**


-


Inbound candidates convert to hires at higher rates because they actively seek your company out.


-


AI-assisted application tools have pushed applicant volumes up, making automated screening a necessity.


-


A consistent phone screen process with a wide net tends to build stronger pipelines and reduce bias.


-


Spreading budget across multiple job boards over time, instead of a single channel, produces better results.


-


Some tools automate job board posting, applicant filtering, and employer brand audits to make inbound workable for lean teams.


## Inbound Recruiting: An Overview


According to[Zippia’s 2026 research](https://www.zippia.com/advice/percentage-of-job-searches-start-on-google/) , 70% of job seekers start their search on Google, and according to Dover’s internal data, roughly 40% of hires made by our customers have come from inbound channels, though this figure can vary by industry and company stage. Inbound recruiting is clearly an important channel for hiring managers and teams, but it differs from outbound and referrals because it involves having candidates “come to you” through the touchpoints you use to attract talent and set yourself apart in the market, such as your company website and job boards.


Qualified inbound candidates are more likely to result in hires than outbound candidates because these candidates are actively searching for a role, and have demonstrated an express interest in your company. Despite this, we’ve seen that as a channel, inbound is often neglected and severely underutilized.


## Inbound Recruiting in 2026


As of 2026, AI-assisted job application tools have made it easier than ever for candidates to apply to dozens of roles with minimal effort, pushing[average applicant volumes per posting](https://thesaaslibrary.com/ai-hiring-doom-loop-2026/) well above what most teams were managing even two years ago. That volume shift has made automated screening less of a nice-to-have and more of a prerequisite for keeping up with inbound without burning out your hiring team. At the same time, a clear and consistent employer brand has become a real filter: candidates sorting through a flood of roles are more likely to engage with companies whose value proposition is visible and specific, which separates teams that invest in employer brand from those that treat it as an afterthought.


## Shortcomings of the Traditional Approach of Managing Inbound


We’ve seen why with our customers firsthand: an inbound strategy is not easy to develop and maintain. It’s traditionally been very difficult to tell, (given the hundreds of job boards that exist), where it makes sense to advertise your job postings, how long you should post your ads for, and how much budget is appropriate. Perhaps the hardest part of all is finding time to manage a large number of inbound applicants to begin with.


Here’s what an inbound strategy, lacking in automation, programmatic job board advertising, and an always-on phone screen process typically looks like:


-


**Limited employer brand:** Your employer brand doesn’t produce sufficient traffic to your website or careers page, so you don’t get the applicants you’re looking for.


-


**Lack of job board familiarity:** You turn to[job boards](https://www.dover.com/blog/top-free-job-posting-sites) to increase the number of applicants for your open roles, but don’t know which ones would make your role successful, and don’t have a good sense of how to create a strategy or budget for them.


-


**Difficulty processing applications:** After some time, you finally get applicants in the door, but it’s hard to[process the high volume of applications](https://www.dover.com/blog/ats-manage-inbound-applications-startup) . It’s noisy, finding a qualified candidate requires a lot of patience and effort, and it’s easy to fall behind.[2026 data from HiringThing](https://blog.hiringthing.com/job-application-statistics) shows the applicant-to-interview ratio has fallen to around 2-3%, meaning most applicants never reach a screening stage.


-


**Overwhelming phone screens:** You might give up after a few unsuccessful phone screens leading to a scheduling backlog and delayed hiring process.


## A New Way to Do Inbound Recruiting


There is a new way to approach inbound: the following suggestions reflect the standard a high-quality inbound strategy requires:


### Build a Strong Employer Brand


In a wildly competitive market for talent, it’s important to stand out from the pack. We use a data-driven approach to measure your[employer brand affinity with candidates](https://www.woodsco.global/news/why-employer-branding-is-now-a-recruitment-strategy-not-a-marketing-exercise/) , and help you with content creation and diversity audits so you can attract high-quality candidates.


### Commit to Job Boards for a Reasonable Amount of Time and Set Aside a Sizeable Budget


Diversifying your[free job posting sites](https://www.dover.com/blog/top-free-job-posting-sites) (and managing the requirements and billing involved in that process) can certainly be time-consuming and difficult. Hiring teams who are patient with the process and spread their efforts across multiple channels tend to be rewarded with good hires.


### Process Applications Quickly


If your inbound strategy is working well, you should expect a steady stream of applicants. It is worth reviewing applications and resumes and starting to build a pipeline of first phone screens. Falling behind on this could mean a growing backlog of applicants, candidates feeling as though their applications are not being considered, and delayed phone screens, resulting in a poor candidate experience or drop off. Using an[ATS to manage inbound applications](https://www.dover.com/blog/ats-manage-inbound-applications-startup) can help keep this process on track for lean teams.


### Cast a Wide, Permissive Net for Phone Screens, and Consider Handing Them Off


Due to the sheer volume of applications a single job posting receives, there’s a tendency for hiring managers to filter on a strict set of criteria and eliminate “time-wasting” conversations with candidates who don’t seem like a perfect fit.


We’ve seen that this is the wrong approach: employers who devote time to a consistent phone screen process with a set of candidates benefit from a healthier pipeline and the ability to screen people out where necessary. This also helps reduce bias, since someone’s job history is not always indicative of the skills needed to function well in a startup environment (being quick and eager to learn, great communicators, or collaborators).


Automated filtering handles the first cut well. But when inbound volume stays high across multiple open roles, or when a role is senior or technically specialized, the coordination burden can outgrow what tooling alone covers. That is the natural inflection point where a[fractional recruiter](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiting-guide) tends to add the most: taking ownership of the phone screen cadence, building the evaluation framework, and keeping the process moving without adding full-time headcount. An ATS manages the pipeline; a fractional recruiter manages the judgment calls inside it.

## FAQs


### What’s the biggest reason inbound recruiting pipelines fail for early-stage teams?


Most inbound pipelines break at the application review stage, not the sourcing stage. When volume climbs and no filtering process exists, hiring managers fall behind, candidates go weeks without a response, and the pipeline stalls before a single phone screen happens. Automated screening that surfaces only candidates matching defined criteria keeps the process moving without requiring more hours from the team.


### Dover vs. manually managing job boards: what’s the actual difference?


Manual job board management means researching platforms individually, guessing at budget allocation, and handling billing across multiple vendors with no unified view. Dover automates posting to relevant boards, surfaces budget guidance based on hiring plans, and lets teams toggle boards on or off with payment handled directly in-app, removing the coordination overhead that typically causes lean teams to abandon multi-channel distribution after a few weeks.


### How do I build a consistent phone screen process without creating a scheduling backlog?


Start with a wide, permissive screening net instead of filtering strictly on job history, since a candidate’s past roles are not always a reliable signal for startup fit. Using a near-always-available interview resource like Dover Interviewer lets teams act on inbound interest quickly, which reduces the gap between application and first contact, the window where candidates most often drop off.


### What is employer brand and why does it affect inbound applicant quality?


Employer brand is the visible signal a company sends about what it’s like to work there, conveyed through its careers page, job descriptions, and public content. As AI-assisted application tools push applicant volumes higher, candidates sorting through many roles tend to engage more with companies whose value proposition is specific and visible. Teams that invest in brand audits, content, and diversity reviews consistently attract higher-quality inbound applicants than those treating employer brand as an afterthought.


### Can a lean startup run a serious inbound recruiting strategy without a dedicated recruiter?


Yes, provided the right automation is in place across three areas: job board distribution, applicant filtering, and phone screen scheduling. Without tooling covering all three, the manual coordination burden typically exceeds what a founder or part-time hiring manager can absorb alongside other responsibilities. Dover is built precisely for this constraint. It covers board posting, candidate filtering through Slack, and interview scheduling so the process stays active even without dedicated recruiting headcount.


## Final Thoughts on Inbound Recruiting


Teams that commit to a consistent[inbound process](https://www.dover.com/) , covering job board distribution, applicant filtering, and a steady phone screen cadence, tend to build stronger candidate pipelines over time. The right tooling makes that process achievable for lean teams, whether each stage is handled manually or with automation supporting the work. Dover is one concrete implementation of this model: a free ATS paired with on-demand fractional recruiters who work inside the same system, so teams can start with software and layer in recruiting capacity when specific roles call for it.
